title: A boot-time probe answers whether local storage can actually be written
outcome: The 無法保存 condition is finally driven by a real signal: a probe that writes a throwaway key, reads it back, and deletes it, reached through the existing storage port rather than around it, plus the queue's existing runtime write failures. SyncIndicator needs no new plumbing to see it.
acceptanceCriteria: `PendingWritesStorage` gains a fourth method that reports whether the store can actually be written; its localStorage implementation performs the write-read-delete and its failure is reported honestly, in the same shape as the existing three methods. The three existing methods are untouched.

`provider.tsx` calls that method once next to `restorePendingWrites`, against the same storage instance, and dispatches the result into `storageUnavailable`. It does not touch `localStorage` itself -- storage details stay behind the port, which is what D1 of `retryable-queue-persistence` built it for.

The existing `catch` around the persistence listener -- kept there deliberately by D4 of `retryable-queue-persistence` -- also sets `storageUnavailable` on a runtime save failure, because the store can become unwritable mid-match even after a successful boot probe.
A successful probe followed by a later runtime failure still surfaces 無法保存: the field is not written once and forgotten.

No new Redux slice, context, or selector is introduced: SyncIndicator's existing `useAppSelector((state) => state.pendingWrites)` picks up `storageUnavailable` because it already reads the whole slice.

The stale comment at the top of `sync-indicator.tsx` describing the component as 'a pure projection of the pending-write queue' is corrected, since it now also reflects a signal that does not come from queue contents.
The probe runs once per mount, not on every render or on every queue change.

The probe's failure path is covered by handing in a storage double that fails, through the parameter `makeStore` and `createPendingWritesPersistence` already accept for exactly this purpose, rather than by mocking the `localStorage` global.
